title: blended-rate-scenarios-scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad: trying to capture some blended-rate ideas that mix per-token generation, per-embedding, and a small per-request (or concurrency) surcharge to better reflect infra costs and smoothing for small customers. Notes are messy — treat as thought-dump.

Goal:
- Find simple pricing primitives that:
  1) reflect true marginal serving costs (infra + network + overhead)
  2) avoid nickel-and-diming for tiny calls (chat UX)
  3) make it easy to predict bill for common usage patterns (search, chat, ingestion)

Assumptions / baseline numbers (very rough internal guesstimates):
- Infra marginal cost for generation (after pooling & batching): ~ $0.002 per 1k tokens served (amortized GPU + power + infra ops).
- Extra overhead (control plane, routing, telemetry) ~ $0.0005 per 1k tokens.
- Embedding marginal cost (dense vector CPU/GPU mix) ~ $0.0009 per 1k tokens-equivalent (or $0.0009 per embedding request if we normalize).
- Request orchestration cost (cold-start, small RPCs) roughly $0.0003 per request on average — varies heavily with model and concurrency.
- Effective caching/batching reduces marginal token cost by ~30% on steady workloads; for bursty interactive it's closer to 0-10%.
- Customer-provided quantized model/Private deploy has ~30-50% lower infra marginals (we should handle different pricing for Private + Dedicated).

Pricing primitives to consider (simple):
- generation_per_1k: $X per 1k output tokens (round to 3 decimals)
- input_token_factor: factor * output_tokens (we bill both input + output tokens)
- per_request: $Y per request (covers orchestration slices) — optional, or replaced by minimum monthly baseline
- embedding_per_vector: $Z per embedding (or per-1k-token-equivalent)
- concurrency_surcharge: small percent of bill when > N concurrent requests (for burst protection)

Blended-rate idea (single line):
- charge a small per-request fee to make small interactive chat calls economic for Redwood, plus a per-1k token generation line that reflects batching benefits. Example: $0.004 per 1k tokens + $0.00075 per request.

Concrete scenario math (toy examples):
Scenario A — Interactive chatbot, 3 turns average, 200 tokens in, 250 tokens out per turn:
- tokens per turn billed = 200 + 250 = 450 tokens
- tokens per session (3 turns) = 3 * 450 = 1350 tokens = 1.35k tokens
- if price = $0.004 / 1k tokens -> token line = 1.35 * $0.004 = $0.0054
- per-request fee = 3 * $0.00075 = $0.00225
- total per session = $0.00765 (~0.76 cents)
- compare to infra marginal cost: 1.35k * $0.002 = $0.0027 + overhead ~ $0.000675 -> ~$0.0034 actual cost. Gross margin ~55%.

Scenario B — Batch document embedding job, 10k docs, 768-d vectors, run as single long job (no many small RPCs):
- if embedding price = $0.004 per 1k-token-equivalent -> not great (we should price embeddings per vector).
- alternate: embedding_per_vector = $0.0009 -> cost to customer = 10,000 * $0.0009 = $9.00
- infra marginal cost (our estimate) = 10,000 * $0.0004 = $4.00 -> margin ~56%

Scenario C — Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline: 1 embed + 1 generation per user query
- embedding per query: $0.0009
- generation: assume 800 tokens total -> 0.8 * $0.004 = $0.0032
- per-request overhead: $0.00075
- total = $0.00485 per query (~0.5 cents)

Notes on meter smoothing / minimums:
- Small interactive calls: per-request fee avoids weirdly tiny bills that under-recover fix costs. But customers hate per-request if it is visible; consider bundling: e.g., include N free requests per month per seat or per API key.
- Alternative: use a monthly baseline (minimum commit) for heavy users and keep pure PAYG for explorers.

Tier ideas (playful, hybrid):
- Explorer (free-tier): 100k tokens / month free + 5k embedding credits + throttled QPS. Purpose: low-friction onboarding.
- Starter PAYG: pay-as-you-go with blended rate (token + request) and no commitments. Good for small apps.
- Growth subscription: monthly committed spend (e.g., $500/mo) -> 10% discount on token line + 1,000 free requests/day.
- Dedicated/Private: negotiated rates (volume + reserved capacity) with lower per-token base and optionally white-glove support fees.

Blended examples (table-in-head) — want these numbers to be intuitive and round:
- Generation base: $0.004 / 1k tokens
- Embeddings: $0.0009 / vector
- Per-request: $0.00075 / request (or included as 1k token equivalent of $0.003 per 1k)
- Volume discounts: 10% @ 100M tokens/mo, 20% @ 1B tokens/mo (we can experiment)

How to present to customers (UX/psych):
- Show major line items: tokens (Xk) and embeddings (Y) — hide per-request fee in "infrastructure surcharge" line or include as free monthly allotment to make invoices friendlier.
- Provide an "estimated monthly bill" calculator in Console that lets engineering input: avg tokens/turn, turns/day, queries/day, and shows SLO tradeoffs (latency vs cost).

Edge cases / hidden complexity:
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming causes many small packets; consider treating streaming sessions with a session-based minimum charge instead of per-request.
- Caching: pinning / prefix caching can drastically reduce effective tokens; encourage customers to enable caching and show them projected savings.
- Model variants: offer a cheaper quantized variant (e.g., q4_0) at 60% of base price; force compatibility/routing rules that fall back automatically.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are our infra marginal cost estimates realistic? need SRE/infra to sanity-check with recent telemetry and region-specific pricing. (TODO: ask infra for 90-day avg marginal cost per 1k tokens by model family) -> linked as JIRA-PRIC-482
- How visible do we make per-request fees vs bundling in token price? UX research required. (ask DEX/growth)
- Consider an "effective per-1k-token" metric that we publish — i.e., for a given archetype show effective cost after average request fees and avg input:output ratios.

Quick variant experiments (A/B ideas):
- A: No per-request fee; generation price = $0.005 / 1k tokens.
- B: Keep generation $0.004 / 1k + per-request $0.00075.
- Run both on new signups for 6 weeks, measure ARPU / churn / support complaints for small customers.

Notes-to-self for implementation:
- Billing engine needs to accept three primitives on metering: token_count, request_count, embedding_count. Support promo credits that can be applied per-primitive.
- Console calc: give "session cost" calculator templates: chat, RAG, embedding-batch.

Random brain dump ends here. Next steps: get SRE infra numbers, sync with growth on messaging, sketch invoice UX, prototype A/B in sandbox.

Unresolved phrasing to clean up for PRD: "blended rate" vs "token + infra surcharge" vs "session-minimum". Pick one and be consistent.

-- Maya
